newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.50 - private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-up $1.50 - private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Monday sold steady to mostly $0.50-$1.00 per cwt higher, instances $1.50 higher, livestock dealers said.
Gains were powered by light marketings and outlooks for sharply higher CME pork complex futures following Friday's USDA quarterly Hogs and Pigs Report, they said.
The report showed a smaller-than-expected number of hogs being held back for breeding purposes as of June 1.
"I think what's happening is guys took a look at that report and decided not to sell too many hogs today because they know prices are going to go up," one Iowa buyer said.
Hogs kept for breeding were pegged at 101 percent of a year ago, below analysts' average pre-report estimate of 104.3 and well below the range of estimates of 103-106, USDA said.

All hogs as of June 1 was estimated by USDA at 102 percent of a year earlier, nearly matching the analyst's average estimate of 102.9 and hogs kept for marketing were 102, also nearly matching its average estimate of 102.6.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hogs sold thinly up $0.50 at $58.50-$59.50 in the country and $59.50-$60.50 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold $1.00-$1.50 higher at $59.50-$60.00 in the country and $60.00-$60.50 at plants.
Indiana hogs were steady at $58.00-$59.00 in the country and $59.00-$60.00 at plants and Ohio hogs were steady at $57.00-$58.00 in the country and $59.00-$60.50 at plants.
